answer:
Set the x grid as x_i = i/60 for i = 0, 1, ..., 60, so dx = 1/60 and there are 61 x points including both Dirichlet boundaries.
Set the y grid as y_j = j/64 for j = 0, 1, ..., 63, so dy = 1/64 and there are 64 periodic y points on [0,1) with no duplicated endpoint.
Use the initial condition u(x,y,0) = sin(pi*x)*cos(2*pi*y) evaluated in radians on this grid.
Apply Dirichlet boundary conditions u(0,y,t)=0 and u(1,y,t)=0 for all y and t.
Apply periodic boundary conditions in y so that index -1 wraps to index 63 and index 64 wraps to index 0.
Discretize the spatial Laplacian with second-order central differences: u_xx uses (u[i+1,j]-2u[i,j]+u[i-1,j])/dx^2 and u_yy uses (u[i,j+1]-2u[i,j]+u[i,j-1])/dy^2 with periodic wrapping in y.
Use implicit Euler time integration with dt = 0.001 for 360 steps to reach T = 0.3.
At each implicit Euler step, solve the linear system (I - dt*0.05*L)*u_new = u_current, where L is the discrete Laplacian and the x boundary values are kept fixed at zero.
Compute the final solution u at T = 0.3 as a 2D array of shape (64, 61) such that u[j,i] corresponds to u(x_i, y_j).
Evaluate the reference solution u_exact(x,y,T) = exp(-0.05*(pi^2 + (2*pi)^2)*T)*sin(pi*x)*cos(2*pi*y) on the same grid.
Save a NumPy .npz file named "solution_agent_heat_16.npz" containing x as a 1D array of length 61, y as a 1D array of length 64, u as a 2D array of shape (64, 61), and scalar metadata T, dx, dy, dt.
Save a heatmap or contour plot of u(x,y,T) as "solution_agent_heat_16.png".
Print min(u), max(u), and the discrete L2 norm sqrt(sum(u^2)*dx*dy) at T.
Compute the error against the reference solution on the same grid and print the maximum absolute error and the L2 error sqrt(sum((u-u_exact)^2)*dx*dy).
